claim: Parameter-based knowledge editing cannot reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities. The near-perfect editing results reported in prior work do not survive realistic evaluation, and the limitation is geometric rather than incidental: localized weight edits are disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space and propagate globally, so damage compounds as edits accumulate. A parameter-free approach that leaves the weights untouched is therefore a serious alternative to parameter editing rather than a fallback.
experiments_evaluated: To address subclaim Can parameter-based knowledge editing reliably update factual knowledge in a large language model without damaging its core capabilities, run a realistic sequential-edit benchmark comparing parameter-modifying editors (ROME, MEMIT if available, MEND, KE, and small-step/constrained fine-tuning) against parameter-free or parameter-preserving alternatives (IKE and, if implementable, SERAC/T-Patcher) on GPT-2 and GPT-J using public COUNTERFACT and ZSRE splits. First filter out unrecallable or trivial instances as the field expects. Evaluate both isolated single-edit rollback and cumulative no-rollback settings with batch sizes 1, 10, 100, 1000 and edit sequences sampled by relation. After each cumulative step, measure Reliability/Efficacy on edited prompts, Generalization on paraphrases/equivalence neighbors, Locality on out-of-scope prompts, plus core-capability probes on HellaSwag, LAMBADA, and Natural Questions relative to the unedited model. Include pre-edit baselines, in-context editing baselines, and cross-dataset replication. The key analysis is whether any parameter-based method maintains high edit success while keeping locality and downstream capability loss near zero under cumulative editing; compare degradation curves as edit count rises. If parameter editors look near-perfect only in rollback single-edit evaluation but lose locality or broader task performance in cumulative settings while parameter-free methods remain stable, that would support the claim. If instead one or more parameter editors maintain strong Reliability/Generalization with negligible locality and capability damage even after many edits, that would weaken the claim substantially. If stronger publicly available evidence already existed reporting cumulative no-rollback results with unrelated-task robustness across multiple editors and backbones, this experiment would be less necessary.

To address subclaim Do the near-perfect editing results reported in prior work survive realistic evaluation, reproduce the headline settings from prior papers on COUNTERFACT and ZSRE for ROME/MEND/KE on GPT-2 and GPT-J, then systematically broaden the evaluation along axes the subfield says are often omitted: equivalence-paraphrase neighborhoods, portability probes (subject-replace, reverse, one-hop where available), sequential no-rollback accumulation, out-of-scope locality, and unrelated robustness tasks. Use the standard COUNTERFACT ES/PS/NS and aggregate score S, plus Reliability/Generalization/Locality definitions by neighborhoods. Compare reported canonical-prompt scores against this expanded suite and run an ablation table showing which evaluation additions reduce apparent performance. To guard against prompt-generation artifacts, validate a random sample of generated probes automatically and manually. Possible conclusions: if near-perfect efficacy remains high across paraphrases, neighborhood probes, portability, and sequential accumulation without harming HellaSwag/LAMBADA/NQ, then the criticism of unrealistic evaluation is not supported. If scores collapse mainly when moving from canonical prompts to paraphrases/neighborhoods or from isolated edits to cumulative edits, that would strongly support the subclaim that prior near-perfect results do not survive realistic evaluation. If direct public benchmark releases already included these expanded probes and cumulative protocols for the same methods, a new reproduction would be less necessary.

To address subclaim Is the limitation of parameter-based knowledge editing geometric rather than incidental, and the related subclaims Are localized weight edits disproportionately amplified along low-variance directions of the model's representation space? and Do localized weight edits propagate globally?, perform a representation-geometry and intervention study on GPT-2 and GPT-J with ROME/MEND/KE edits localized using both causal tracing and representation zeroing. For a large sample of editable facts from COUNTERFACT and ZSRE, collect hidden states at candidate edit layers for subject-token positions over a broad natural-text corpus or held-out benchmark prompts, estimate the covariance eigenspectrum of those representations, and decompose each induced hidden-state change or effective weight-update action into principal-component coordinates. Test whether edit effects have disproportionate projection or output amplification in low-variance eigendirections, for example by relating component variance rank to resulting logit change, edit success, and collateral changes on unrelated prompts. Then measure global propagation by tracing post-edit activation differences across all layers/tokens on both edited and out-of-scope prompts, quantifying spread beyond the targeted module, and regress collateral damage on low-variance-direction amplification while controlling for layer and editor. Include layer sweeps, corruption-magnitude sensitivity, token aggregation variants, and path-specific analyses that separate MLP from attention routes where feasible. If low-variance components consistently produce outsized downstream logit shifts and predict broader activation spread and locality failure across editors and datasets, that would support a geometric mechanism. If amplification is not concentrated in low-variance directions, or if propagation/damage is explained mainly by particular layers, editors, or tracing choices, then the geometric claim is weakened and the limitation may be more incidental. If prior work had already released multi-model eigenspectrum analyses linking edit vectors to collateral damage with controls for layer and method, this experiment could be partly unnecessary.
reference_experiments: Fix the measurement floor and the inference protocol before editing anything. Score the unedited model on the editing benchmark to establish the pre-edit baseline, and re-run single-edit evaluation of existing methods under plain autoregressive decoding rather than the teacher-forced protocol prior work used, since teacher forcing supplies the ground-truth answer tokens at inference and inflates every number. If methods keep their near-perfect single-edit scores under honest decoding there is no discrepancy to explain. The authors report a pre-edit baseline of Reliability 3.00, Generalization 3.00, Locality 15.50, Portability 4.36 on ZsRE, and a best parameter-based single-edit average of 25.99.

Validate the scoring instrument before quoting any number from it. Judge semantic consistency of generated answers with a strong LLM across reliability, generalization, locality and portability, then cross-check that ranking with a deterministic token-level measure (match ratio and exact match) that does not depend on a model's opinion. If the two disagree, every result is an artifact of the judge rather than a property of the editing methods. The authors find the token-level check reproduces the semantic ranking, with the pre-edit model at 100% by definition and GRACE holding 100% under both single and sequential editing.

Test the asserted mechanism directly. Take the SVD of the original hidden-representation matrix, compute the directional relative change rate R_k = sqrt(n)|u_k^T delta_h| / sigma_k for each principal direction after an edit, and check where amplification concentrates and how it behaves as edits accumulate. The claim's causal story requires R_k > 1 predominantly in low-singular-value directions with the fraction rising monotonically with edit count, across methods and architectures.

Run the main benchmark. Compare eleven editing methods spanning locate-then-edit (ROME, MEMIT, PMET, RECT, AlphaEdit, FT-L), meta-learning (MEND), additional-parameter (AdaLoRA, WISE) and external-memory (GRACE, SCR) families, under sequential editing at 1, 10, 100 and full-dataset edit counts, on ZsRE and WikiData-counterfact, across Llama-2-7B-Chat, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, reporting all four dimensions. The claim holds if every parameter-modifying method degrades toward zero as edits accumulate and the parameter-free retrieval baseline outscores all of them; the authors report ROME, RECT, FT-L, MEND and AdaLoRA at 0.00-0.25 average under sequential editing on DeepSeek-R1-Distill, against SCR at 56.59 single and 60.19 sequential.

Measure damage to capabilities the edits never targeted. Take the models edited in the main benchmark and evaluate them on mathematical reasoning (AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC, OlympiadBench, MATH-500) and broad benchmarks (GPQA-Diamond, ARC-c, MMLU-Pro), reporting accuracy after 10 and after 100 sequential edits. Without this the study would only show editing is ineffective, not that it is damaging. The authors report ROME and RECT losing 2.74 and 8.37 average accuracy at 10 edits and falling to near zero at 100, with MEND at 0.00 after both.

Rule out that the result is an artifact of scale, knowledge type, fact difficulty or one method's configuration. Repeat the sweep on larger models (Llama-2-13B, Qwen3-14B), on event-level knowledge (ELKEN, with events converted to triples for the parameter-based arms), split by high- and low-confidence fact sets, and probe the hyperparameter and architecture sensitivity of AlphaEdit — the one method that does not collapse — including its failure to run on Llama-2 and Mistral. If the collapse disappears at 13-14B or only occurs on triple-shaped facts, the claim is bounded rather than general.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A pre-edit reference point and an inference protocol that measures ordinary generated answers without supplying the target tokens, allowing single-edit results to be compared against both the clean floor and the inflated teacher-forced results.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed 0 includes pre-edit baselines and isolated single-edit evaluation within a realistic sequential protocol; proposed 1 reproduces the canonical headline settings and compares them with an expanded evaluation. Together these would let the team determine whether apparently near-perfect single-edit performance survives ordinary generation and establish the unedited reference point.

reference_coverage.adequacy: Validation of the outcome measure through agreement between a semantic assessment of answer consistency and an independent deterministic token-level assessment, so method rankings are not attributable to the scorer.
reference_coverage.rationale: The proposed set uses efficacy/reliability and standard benchmark scores, and manually or automatically checks whether generated probes are valid, but it never scores the same generated answers with both an independent semantic evaluator and deterministic match/exact-match measures and tests their ranking agreement. The proposed team would not learn whether the scoring instrument itself is producing an artifact.
reasoning_chain: [1] The reference experiment establishes scorer validity by comparing semantic judgments with deterministic token-level outcomes on the same edits.
[2] Proposed experiments 0 and 1 report editing scores and validate generated probes, but probe validation is not an independent cross-check of answer-scoring semantics against token matches.
[3] Therefore the proposed outcomes could show method performance without revealing whether semantic-versus-token scoring disagreement is responsible for the ranking.
[4] A team running the proposed set would fail to learn what reference experiment 1 would have told them: whether the scoring instrument, rather than the editing methods, is driving the results.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A direct, normalized measurement of how representation changes are distributed across variance-ranked directions, tested over increasing edit counts and across editing methods and architectures, together with evidence that the directional pattern accounts for global collateral effects.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed 2 directly studies covariance eigendirections, low-variance amplification, activation spread on unrelated prompts, and controls for layers, editors, routes, and tracing choices. Proposed 0 supplies cumulative edit counts and degradation curves. However, proposed 2 is written around the change from an individual edit and does not explicitly require the normalized directional amplification statistic to be recomputed after cumulative edit counts or test the required monotonic rise in the fraction of over-amplified low-variance directions. The team would have evidence for the geometric association and global propagation, but the accumulation-dependent mechanism would remain ambiguous.
reasoning_chain: [1] The reference experiment tests not only low-variance amplification but also whether its prevalence increases monotonically as edits accumulate, across methods and architectures.

[2] Proposed 2 measures low-variance projections and global activation propagation, while proposed 0 measures cumulative performance damage, but neither explicitly links a repeated variance-normalized directional measurement to the 1/10/100/1000 cumulative states.
[3] Performance degradation with edit count does not by itself establish that the geometric amplification pattern is the cause or that the fraction of amplified directions rises monotonically.
[4] Thus the proposed set would fail to determine the full accumulation-dependent geometric mechanism that reference experiment 2 would have established.

reference_coverage.adequacy: A comparative sequential evaluation of multiple weight-changing and weight-preserving editing families across more than one model architecture and factual benchmark, at increasing edit counts, using efficacy, generalization, locality, portability, and cumulative-degradation comparisons.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed 0 compares several parameter-modifying editors with parameter-free or parameter-preserving alternatives across two backbones, two factual benchmarks, and edit counts through 1000, measuring reliability, generalization, locality, and capability effects. Proposed 1 adds portability, canonical-versus-expanded evaluation, and no-rollback accumulation. This has comparable discriminating power for deciding whether parameter editors systematically lose effectiveness/locality under accumulation while a weight-preserving alternative remains competitive; the reference's particular method count, model names, and exact full-dataset setting are not binding elements of the claim.

reference_coverage.adequacy: An untargeted-capability evaluation of edited models against their unedited versions after moderate and heavy sequential editing, using multiple unrelated reasoning and general-knowledge tasks to distinguish editing failure from collateral capability damage.
reference_coverage.rationale: Proposed 0 explicitly measures HellaSwag, LAMBADA, and Natural Questions relative to the unedited model after each cumulative editing step, including the 10- and 100-edit regimes. These unrelated capability probes would reveal whether successful or unsuccessful edits cause collateral degradation; the particular collection of mathematics and broad benchmarks in the reference is not required by the claim.

reference_coverage.adequacy: Stress testing over model scale, factual-knowledge representation and difficulty strata, and implementation choices, including sensitivity of the strongest non-collapsing method to hyperparameters and architecture.
reference_coverage.rationale: The proposed set provides some robustness through two backbones, two datasets, relation-sampled edit sequences, multiple editors, cross-dataset replication, and probe validation. It does not test substantially larger models, event-level knowledge, explicit confidence/difficulty strata, or the hyperparameter and architecture sensitivity of the strongest exception (and it does not include that exception in the proposed editor set). Consequently the observed collapse could still be a scale, knowledge-type, difficulty, or configuration artifact.
reasoning_chain: [1] The reference experiment is designed to rule out several alternative explanations for collapse: model scale, knowledge type, fact difficulty, and editor configuration, especially for the method that appears not to collapse.

[2] Proposed experiments 0 and 1 vary backbones, datasets, relations, and editor families, which addresses some heterogeneity but does not include a larger-model sweep, event-level facts, explicit confidence strata, or sensitivity analysis of the strongest surviving method.

[3] Without those tests, stable or unstable behavior in the proposed runs cannot distinguish a general limitation from a limitation specific to the selected scales, fact formats, difficulty mix, or configurations.
[4] The proposed team would fail to learn the generality and exception-sensitivity that reference experiment 5 would have provided.

sufficiency_reasoning: The proposed set would substantially test realistic cumulative editing, untargeted capability damage, and global/low-variance geometric effects, and it would provide a useful multi-method comparison with a weight-preserving alternative. It would not validate the scoring instrument through semantic/token-level agreement, and its geometry study does not explicitly establish the required monotonic accumulation of normalized low-variance amplification. Robustness across larger scales, event-level knowledge, difficulty strata, and the strongest exceptional editor is also incomplete. Those gaps leave parts of the claim—especially the full geometric causal story and its generality—unsettled.
missing: A paired semantic-judge versus deterministic token-level scoring validation on the same outputs, with ranking agreement reported.

A cumulative geometry sweep recomputing variance-normalized directional amplification at each edit count and testing whether low-variance over-amplification increases monotonically across methods and architectures.

Robustness experiments on substantially larger models, event-level facts, explicit high/low-confidence or difficulty strata, and hyperparameter/architecture sensitivity of the strongest surviving parameter-based editor.
